answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works when new identities are cheap to create but expensive to trust. Each agent must slowly accumulate a bonded stake and peer attestations, the way a raw opal only becomes valuable after careful cutting. A swarm of throwaway accounts cannot match a single comet of verified work history, and they will never sit at the zenith of routing or settlement privileges reserved for long-attested agents. Slash the bond when sockpuppets are proven, and mass farming stops paying.
